23278-janice-day-at-poketown.title: Janice Day At Poketown
23278-janice-day-at-poketown.creator: Helen Beecher Long
23278-janice-day-at-poketown.description: A book by Helen Beecher Long. The officious man in the blue cap on the dock had shouted "All aboard!" the moment the passengers left the cars of the little narrow-gauge railroad, on which the girl had been riding for more than two hours; but it was some minutes before the wheezy old steamer got under way.

arxiv-2008-12139.title: A Two-level ADMM Algorithm for AC OPF with Global Convergence Guarantees
arxiv-2008-12139.creator: Kaizhao Sun, Xu Andy Sun
arxiv-2008-12139.description: Abstract This paper proposes a two-level distributed algorithmic framework for solving the AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem with convergence guarantees. The presence of highly nonconvex constraints in OPF poses significant challenges to distributed algorithms based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). In particular, convergence is not provably guaranteed for nonconvex network optimization problems like AC OPF.

arxiv-2012-06980.title: GeoNet++: Iterative Geometric Neural Network with Edge-Aware Refinement for Joint Depth and Surface Normal Estimation
arxiv-2012-06980.creator: Xiaojuan Qi, Zhengzhe Liu, Renjie Liao, Philip H. S. Torr, Raquel Urtasun, and Jiaya Jia
arxiv-2012-06980.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a geometric neural network with edge-aware refinement (GeoNet++) to jointly predict both depth and surface normal maps from a single image. Building on top of two-stream CNNs, GeoNet++ captures the geometric relationships between depth and surface normals with the proposed depth-to-normal and normal-to-depth modules.

arxiv-2201-02887.title: Simple Algebraic Proofs of Uniqueness for Erdős-Ko-Rado Theorems
arxiv-2201-02887.creator: Yuval Filmus, Nathan Lindzey
arxiv-2201-02887.description: Abstract We give simpler algebraic proofs of uniqueness for several Erdős-Ko-Rado results, i.e., that the canonically intersecting families are the only largest intersecting families. Using these techniques, we characterize the largest partially 2-intersecting families of perfect hypermatchings, resolving a recent conjecture of Meagher, Shirazi, and Stevens.

arxiv-2206-05140.title: Evolution of a Relativistic Outflow and X-ray Corona in the Extreme Changing-Look AGN 1ES 1927+654 Facilities: XMM-Newton , NuSTAR , NICER XSPEC ( Arnaud 1996 ) , Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ) , xillver ( García & Kallman 2010 ; García et al. 2013
arxiv-2206-05140.creator: Megan Masterson, Erin Kara, Claudio Ricci, Javier A. García, Andrew C. Fabian, Ciro Pinto, Peter Kosec, Ronald A. Remillard, Michael Loewenstein, Benny Trakhtenbrot, Iair Arcavi
arxiv-2206-05140.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Megan Masterson, Erin Kara, Claudio Ricci, Javier A. García, Andrew C. Fabian, Ciro Pinto, Peter Kosec, Ronald A. Remillard, Michael Loewenstein, Benny Trakhtenbrot, Iair Arcavi. 1ES 1927+654 is a paradigm-defying AGN and one of the most peculiar X-ray nuclear transients. In early 2018, this well-known AGN underwent a changing-look event, in which broad optical emission lines appeared and the optical flux increased.

arxiv-2207-07613.title: Improved Algorithms for Recognizing Perfect Graphs and Finding Shortest Odd and Even Holes
arxiv-2207-07613.creator: Yung-Chung Chiu, Kai-Yuan Lai, Hsueh-I Lu
arxiv-2207-07613.description: Abstract An induced subgraph of an n n -vertex graph G G is a graph that can be obtained by deleting a set of vertices together with its incident edges from G G . A hole of G G is an induced cycle of G G with length at least four.

arxiv-2303-10982.title: In search for infalling clumps in molecular clouds
arxiv-2303-10982.creator: Zhibo Jiang, Shaobo Zhang, Zhiwei Chen, Yang Yang, Shuling Yu, Haoran Feng, Ji Yang, the MWISP group
arxiv-2303-10982.description: Abstract We have started a systematic survey of molecular clumps with infall motions to study the very early phase of star formation. Our first step is to utilize the data products by MWISP to make an unbiased survey for blue asymmetric line profiles of CO isotopical molecules.

arxiv-2305-09090.title: BOSS - Biomarker Optimal Segmentation System
arxiv-2305-09090.creator: Liuyi Lan, Xuanjin Cheng, Li Xing \ORCID 0000-0002-4186-7909, Xuekui Zhang \ORCID 0000-0003-4728-2343
arxiv-2305-09090.description: Abstract Motivation: Precision medicine is a major trend in the future of medicine. It aims to provide tailored medical treatment and prevention strategies based on an individual’s unique characteristics and needs. Biomarker is the primary source of patients’ unique features used in precision medicine.

arxiv-2306-00964.title: Cocktail : Mixing Multi-Modality Controls for Text-Conditional Image Generation
arxiv-2306-00964.creator: Minghui Hu, Jianbin Zheng, Daqing Liu, Chuanxia Zheng, Chaoyue Wang, Dacheng Tao, Tat-Jen Cham
arxiv-2306-00964.description: Abstract Text-conditional diffusion models are able to generate high-fidelity images with diverse contents. However, linguistic representations frequently exhibit ambiguous descriptions of the envisioned objective imagery, requiring the incorporation of additional control signals to bolster the efficacy of text-guided diffusion models.

arxiv-2311-08883.title: Distilling Rule-based Knowledge into Large Language Models
arxiv-2311-08883.creator: Wenkai Yang, Yankai Lin, Jie Zhou, Ji-Rong Wen
arxiv-2311-08883.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown incredible performance in completing various real-world tasks. The current paradigm of knowledge learning for LLMs is mainly based on learning from examples , in which LLMs learn the internal rule implicitly from a certain number of supervised examples.

arxiv-2401-05804.title: A Microscopic study of Magnetic monopoles in Topological Insulators
arxiv-2401-05804.creator: Yoshiyuki Matsuki
arxiv-2401-05804.description: Abstract In this article, we analyze a magnetic monopole in topological insulators. The monopole obtain a fractional electric charge because of the Witten effect. We consider this system with a microscopic view by adding the Wilson term to the ordinary Dirac Hamiltonian.

arxiv-2401-08818.title: Link Me Baby One More Time: Social Music Discovery on Spotify
arxiv-2401-08818.creator: Shazia’Ayn Babul, Desislava Hristova, Antonio Lima, Renaud Lambiotte, Mariano Beguerisse-Díaz
arxiv-2401-08818.description: Abstract We explore the social and contextual factors that influence the outcome of person-to-person music recommendations and discovery. Specifically, we use data from Spotify to investigate how a link sent from one user to another results in the receiver engaging with the music of the shared artist.

arxiv-2406-01036.title: Remarks on the geometric structure of port-Hamiltonian systems
arxiv-2406-01036.creator: Jonas Kirchhoff, Bernhard Maschke
arxiv-2406-01036.description: Abstract Abstract We study the geometric structure of port-Hamiltonian systems. Starting with the intuitive understanding that port-Hamiltonian systems are “in between” certain closed Hamiltonian systems, the geometric structure of port-Hamiltonian systems must be “in between” the geometric structures of the latter systems. These are Courant algebroids; and hence the geometric structures should be related by Courant algebroid morphisms.

arxiv-2406-15415.title: Map-making Strategies For Next Generation CMB Polarization Experiments
arxiv-2406-15415.creator: Simon Biquard
arxiv-2406-15415.description: Abstract I briefly review some of the most common map-making strategies for experiments targeting the polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), in light of the anticipated volumes of data collected by next generation observatories such as Simons Observatory and CMB-S4. Then, I focus on the pair-differencing approach, used for example in the POLARBEAR and BICEP collaborations.

arxiv-2410-01679.title: VinePPO: Refining Credit Assignment in RL Training of LLMs
arxiv-2410-01679.creator: Amirhossein Kazemnejad, Milad Aghajohari, Eva Portelance, Alessandro Sordoni, Siva Reddy, Aaron Courville, Nicolas Le Roux
arxiv-2410-01679.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to complex reasoning tasks that require executing several complex steps before receiving any reward. Properly assigning credit to these steps is essential for enhancing model performance. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), a common reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm used for LLM finetuning, employs value networks to tackle credit assignment.

arxiv-2410-15326.title: A Survey of Uncertainty Estimation in LLMs: Theory Meets Practice
arxiv-2410-15326.creator: Hsiu-Yuan Huang, Yutong Yang, Zhaoxi Zhang, Sanwoo Lee, Yunfang Wu
arxiv-2410-15326.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) continue to evolve, understanding and quantifying the uncertainty in their predictions is critical for enhancing application credibility. However, the existing literature relevant to LLM uncertainty estimation often relies on heuristic approaches, lacking systematic classification of the methods.

arxiv-2502-00243.title: A Fast Periodicity Detection Algorithm Sensitive to Arbitrary Waveforms
arxiv-2502-00243.creator: Douglas P. Finkbeiner, Thomas A. Prince, Samuel E. Whitebook
arxiv-2502-00243.description: Abstract A reexamination of period finding algorithms is prompted by new large area astronomical sky surveys that can identify billions of individual sources having a thousand or more observations per source. This large increase in data necessitates fast and efficient period detection algorithms.

arxiv-2508-14886.title: Particle Injection in 3D Relativistic Magnetic Reconnection Released August 10, 2026
arxiv-2508-14886.creator: Omar French, Omar French \aff 1 \corresp, Gregory R. Werner \aff 1, Dmitri A. Uzdensky \aff 2
arxiv-2508-14886.description: Abstract Relativistic magnetic reconnection has been proposed as an important nonthermal particle acceleration (NTPA) mechanism that generates power-law spectra and high-energy emissions. Power-law particle spectra are in general characterized by three parameters: the power-law index, the high-energy cutoff, and the low-energy cutoff (i.e., the injection energy).

arxiv-2510-21399.title: Projective limits in Euclidean quantum field theory, II: Abelian gauge theory
arxiv-2510-21399.creator: Svetoslav Zahariev
arxiv-2510-21399.description: Abstract . We present two constructions of continuum and thermodynamic limits of Abelian polyhedral gauge theories in arbitrary spacetime dimension. The first construction relies on the existence of projective systems of heat kernel measures, while the second involves an infinite dimensional heat kernel measure defined using projective limit of Hilbert spaces.

arxiv-2602-22532.title: Coarse-to-Fine Learning of Dynamic Causal Structures
arxiv-2602-22532.creator: Dezhi Yang, Qiaoyu Tan, Carlotta Domeniconi, Jun Wang, Lizhen Cui, Guoxian Yu
arxiv-2602-22532.description: Abstract Learning the dynamic causal structure of time series is a challenging problem. Most existing approaches rely on distributional or structural invariance to uncover underlying causal dynamics, assuming stationary or partially stationary causality. However, these assumptions often conflict with the complex, time-varying causal relationships observed in real-world systems.

Strategies that limit the development of resistance and minimize host side-effec

pmc-10596833.title: Psychosocial determinants of adherence to COVID-19 preventive behaviors
pmc-10596833.creator: K Gali, B Hermanns, I Sabat, S Neumann-Böhme, J Schreyögg
pmc-10596833.description: BackgroundNon-adherence to medical guidelines is associated with suboptimal health outcomes and increased healthcare costs, and yet adherence to preventive therapies is often difficult to achieve. Understanding which factors can improve adherence is a public health priority. In this study, we examined the association of psychosocial factors and adherence of preventive behaviors within the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-10632683.title: Limited Polymorphism in the Dihydrofolate Reductase (dhfr) and dihydropteroate synthase genes (dhps) of Plasmodium knowlesi isolate from Thailand
pmc-10632683.creator: Raweewan Sangsri, Kiattawee Choowongkomon, Runch Tuntipaiboontana, Rungniran Sugaram, Patcharida Boondej, Prayuth Sudathip, Arjen M Dondorp, Mallika Imwong
pmc-10632683.description: Highlights•A novel PCR protocol was developed to detect pkdhps polymorphisms.•The R34L pkdhfr and quadruple pkdhps mutations are the most prevalent in Thailand.•Molecular docking showed five pkdhps mutations were less likely to induce drug resistance.•It was suggested that eastern Thailand's isolates are closely related to Cambodia.

pmc-11642403.title: Airborne-Particle Abrasion vs. Hydrofluoric Acid Etching of Dental Ceramics: Impact on the Tensile Bond Strength
pmc-11642403.creator: Valerie Lankes, Andrea Coldea, John Meinen, Falk Schwendicke, Bogna Stawarczyk
pmc-11642403.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study evaluated whether airborne-particle abrasion could be an alternative to hydrofluoric acid etching as a pretreatment for the adhesive bonding of silicate ceramic restorations. Feldspar (FEL; n = 100), lithium silicate (LiSi; n = 100), and zirconia (ZrO2; (n = 80) substrates were CAD/CAM-fabricated and airborne-particle-abraded with Al2O3 (25 µm or 50 µm of mean particle size) at pressures of 0.05 or 0.1 MPa. The controls included FEL (60 s) and LiSi (20 s) etched with hydrofluoric acid.

pmc-12608565.creator: Hadar Sandler Rahat, Tal Friehmann, Marva Dahan Shemesh, Shlomit Tamir, Eli Atar, Tzippy Shochat, Arnon Makori, Ahuva Grubstein, Alberto Signore, Andrea Ciarmiello

These systems were mostly investigated by control trials using cancer-enriched datasets and multiple readers.

pmc-13390694.creator: Kimberly B. Garza, Heqin Yang, Alexicia Richardson, Cheryl Seals, Gary Hawkins, Chad G. Rose, Willliam B. Nowell, Kelly Gavigan, Patrick Stewart, Liana Fraenkel, Jeffrey R. Curtis
